docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Maintainers release. The version is __version__ in injectq/__init__.py (read by hatch). A release updates the version and the changelog, builds with make build (uv build), publishes with make publish (checks with twine, then uploads), and tags the release on GitHub.

InjectQ follows Semantic Versioning. Deprecated names keep working for one minor release with a DeprecationWarning before removal.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
InjectQ logs to the standard logging logger named injectq. It has a NullHandler, so nothing is printed until you configure it.

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger("injectq")      # same object as `from injectq import logger`
handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("[%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s"))
logger.addHandler(handler)
logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

Use logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG) or your application's own logging configuration instead if you already have one. The logger records binding and module installation at DEBUG and INFO; resolution errors are raised as exceptions, not only logged.

docs.title: Upgrading from 0.5 to 0.6
docs.text: InjectQ 0.6 rewrites the resolution engine, the scopes and the context handling. Most code keeps working. This page lists every change that can break code or behave differently.

docs.title: Upgrade in four steps
docs.text:
1. Install 0.6 and run your tests with deprecation warnings turned into errors, so you see every old name:

    pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning

  2. Rename deprecated names using the table below. They still work in 0.6 and are removed in 0.7.

  3. Replace removed names using the removed names table. These raise ImportError or AttributeError now.
  4. Read Behaviour changes and Things that now raise. These are the changes that do not show up as an import error.

Two bugs drive most of the changes: the "current container" was shared by all asyncio tasks on a thread, and a FastAPI request container was invisible to InjectQ.get_instance() and @inject. Both are covered under Behaviour changes.

docs.title: Deprecated names
docs.text:
These work in 0.6, emit a DeprecationWarning when used, and are removed in 0.7.

Old name New name Where injectq.testing.test_container injectq.testing.isolated_container testing injectq.testing.TestModule injectq.testing.MockModule testing injectq.testing.pytest_container_fixture injectq.testing.container_fixture testing InjectAPI InjectFastAPI injectq.integrations.fastapi InjectTask InjectTaskiq injectq.integrations.taskiq get_injector_instance_taskiq get_container_taskiq injectq.integrations.taskiq InjectMCP InjectFastMCP injectq.integrations.fastmcp setup_mcp setup_fastmcp injectq.integrations.fastmcp get_container_mcp get_container_fastmcp injectq.integrations.fastmcp injectq.components (the whole module) no replacement; use modules, providers and container bindings Component, ComponentBinding, ComponentContainer, ComponentError, ComponentInterface, ComponentRegistry, ComponentScope, ComponentState (from injectq) same as above InjectQ(thread_safe=...) remove the argument deprecated: accepted, ignored, warns InjectQ(use_async_scopes=...) remove the argument deprecated: accepted, ignored, warns

The testing names changed because pytest collects anything named test_* or Test* that you import into a test module.

# Before (0.5)
from injectq.testing import test_container, TestModule, pytest_container_fixture

container = pytest_container_fixture()

def test_x():
    with test_container() as c:
        c.install_module(TestModule())

# After (0.6)
from injectq.testing import isolated_container, MockModule, container_fixture

container = container_fixture()

def test_x():
    with isolated_container() as c:
        c.install_module(MockModule())

container_fixture(name="container") takes the fixture name, so container_fixture(name="di") gives a fixture called di.

thread_safe= and use_async_scopes= do nothing now. They are deprecated: still accepted, but passing either emits a DeprecationWarning ("accepted and ignored since 0.6, will be removed in 0.7"). InjectQ() stays silent. Reads never take a lock, and creating a singleton or a scoped instance is always safe under threads and tasks.

# Before (0.5)
container = InjectQ(thread_safe=True, use_async_scopes=True)

# After (0.6)
container = InjectQ()

docs.title: Removed names
docs.text:
These are gone. Importing them raises ImportError (or AttributeError for attributes). We found no uses outside InjectQ itself.

Removed What to do injectq.core.thread_safety: HybridLock, ThreadSafeDict, AsyncSafeCounter, ThreadSafetyMixin, thread_safe Use threading.Lock and plain dicts. The container no longer needs them injectq.core.thread_safe_resolver: ThreadSafeDependencyResolver Use InjectQ. It is always safe injectq.core.async_scopes: AsyncScope, AsyncScopeManager, HybridScope, AsyncRequestScope, AsyncActionScope, HybridRequestScope, HybridActionScope Use container.async_scope("request") injectq.core.async_scopes: request_id_var, user_id_var, get_request_id, set_request_id, get_user_id, set_user_id, request_context, async_request_context Keep your own ContextVars, or bind a @scoped service that holds the ids injectq.core.base_scope_manager: BaseScopeManager; create_enhanced_scope_manager Use container.scope(...) and container.async_scope(...) injectq.core.scopes: SingletonScope, TransientScope, ThreadLocalScope, RequestScope, ActionScope Use bind(..., scope="singleton" / "transient" / "request" / "action") ScopeManager.get_scope() Use container.scope(name) to enter a scope. current_exit_stack(name) gives the active scope's exit stack scope names "async_request" and "async_action" Use "request" and "action". One scope works for sync and async code DependencyResolver.resolve, resolve_async, validate_dependencies, get_dependency_graph, compile_resolution_plans Use container.get, aget, validate, get_dependency_graph, compile. On the resolver: compile_sync, compile_async, node, validate, compile_all, dependency_graph injectq.utils: resolve_forward_ref, Injected, is_concrete_type, get_type_name, safe_issubclass, is_injectable_function, ThreadLocalStorage Use typing.get_type_hints, inspect, issubclass, and Inject[...] injectq.utils.protocols: Resolvable, InjectableFunction, InjectableAsyncFunction, AsyncInjectableCallable They were never used by the container. Remove them injectq.utils.helpers: duplicate format_type_name Use injectq.utils.helpers.format_type_name injectq.diagnostics.validation: MissingDependencyError, InvalidBindingError, TypeMismatchError and the validator's private helpers DependencyValidator.validate() returns a ValidationResult. Catch InjectionError from container.validate() injectq.integrations.fastapi._request_container Use get_container_fastapi() 
# Before (0.5)
from injectq.core.scopes import ThreadLocalScope
from injectq.core.async_scopes import AsyncScopeManager, HybridScope

# After (0.6): no import needed
with container.scope("request"):
    ...
async with container.async_scope("request"):
    ...

docs.title: The current container is per task and per thread
docs.text:
The "current container" (what InjectQ.get_instance(), @inject and the decorators use) is stored in a ContextVar.

  • ContainerContext.set_current(c) and c.activate() apply to the current task or thread, and to everything started from it afterwards: asyncio.create_task, asyncio.to_thread, anyio worker threads.
  • They do not apply to sibling tasks that are already running.
  • A plain threading.Thread and loop.run_in_executor do not inherit it. They see the global container.
  • set_current() and activate() now return a token. ContainerContext.reset_current(token) restores the previous value.
# Before (0.5): set_current() changed the container for every task on the thread
ContainerContext.set_current(container)
await asyncio.gather(job_a(), job_b())

# After (0.6): activate before you start the tasks, and restore when you are done
token = container.activate()
try:
    await asyncio.gather(job_a(), job_b())   # both tasks see `container`
finally:
    ContainerContext.reset_current(token)

# Or, simpler:
with container.context():
    await asyncio.gather(job_a(), job_b())

If your code relied on one task activating a container for another, already running task, change it to activate before the task starts, or pass the container explicitly. See Context and concurrency.

docs.title: Inside FastAPI, FastMCP and Taskiq, get_instance() is the app's container
docs.text:
In 0.5, code in a route that called InjectQ.get_instance() or used @inject got the global container, not the one you passed to setup_fastapi. In 0.6 it gets the container you passed. Each request, MCP message or Taskiq task also gets its own "request" scope.

app_container = InjectQ()
setup_fastapi(app_container, app)

@inject
def helper(repo: Repo): ...

@app.get("/")
def route():
    return helper()
# 0.5: helper() looked in the GLOBAL container, so Repo had to be bound there
# 0.6: helper() uses app_container

If you had bindings only in the global container and relied on @inject helpers finding them, bind them in the container you pass to setup_*.

Exception: the body of a sync (def) Taskiq task runs in run_in_executor, where the container is not current. InjectTaskiq(...) parameters still work. See Taskiq.

docs.title: Request scope is per block
docs.text:
A with container.scope("request"): block now creates a fresh scope and closes it on exit.

# Before (0.5): both blocks could return the same instance,
# and a request-scoped service also worked outside any block
with container.scope("request"):
    a = container[Session]
with container.scope("request"):
    b = container[Session]       # same object as `a`

# After (0.6)
with container.scope("request"):
    a = container[Session]
with container.scope("request"):
    b = container[Session]
assert a is not b
container[Session]               # ScopeError: no active 'request' scope

More scope rules:

  • Nested scopes of the same name restore the outer one on exit. In 0.5, leaving the inner block wiped the outer one.
  • asyncio.to_thread inside a scope sees the caller's scope and gets the same instances.
  • Scopes belong to one container. Two containers never share instances.
  • An instance bound with bind_instance(Key, obj, scope="request") is always returned as is.
  • container.scope("singleton") and container.scope("transient") do nothing.
  • A scope exit runs teardown callbacks in reverse order (last pushed, first run) and passes them the exception, if any. It never suppresses the exception.

See Scopes and Scoped services.

docs.title: Custom scopes: register the name
docs.text:
register_scope takes only a name. It no longer accepts a scope object that does work. If you pass a Scope object, only its name is used.

# Before (0.5)
container._scope_manager.register_scope("job", JobScope())

# After (0.6)
container.register_scope("job")

@scoped("job")
class JobContext: ...

with container.scope("job"):
    ctx = container[JobContext]

Entering a scope name that is not "request", "action" or registered raises ScopeError: Unknown scope.

container.clear_scope(name) drops the instances of that scope. It does not run the scope's exit stack. Leave the with block to run teardowns.

docs.title: aget() honours scopes and creates singletons once
docs.text: In 0.5, await container.aget(Key) ignored the binding scope. Singletons were created again on every call and differed from get(). In 0.6, aget and get return the same singleton, and a scoped key is cached in the active scope. Under concurrency, a singleton is created once, for sync and async code.

docs.title: get() on a key that needs an async factory raises
docs.text:
async def make_db() -> Database: ...
container.bind_factory(Database, make_db)

# Before (0.5): returned an un-awaited coroutine
db = container.get(Database)

# After (0.6)
container.get(Database)            # InjectionError: ... use aget()
db = await container.aget(Database)

If the async part already exists as a singleton or scoped instance, get() still works. aget(UnboundClass) no longer returns a coroutine either.

docs.title: One provider map: the later registration wins
docs.text:
A class binding and a factory for the same key used to live in separate maps, and the factory always won. Now the last registration wins, and allow_override=False rejects the second one whichever kind it is.

container.bind_factory(Mailer, make_test_mailer)
container.bind(Mailer, SmtpMailer)

container.get(Mailer)   # 0.5: make_test_mailer (a factory always won)
                        # 0.6: SmtpMailer (registered last)

In 0.5 a factory always won, whatever the order. In 0.6 the order decides. bind, bind_instance and bind_factory all follow this rule. Re-binding a key also drops that key's cached singleton, so the next get builds a new one.

docs.title: override() is local to the context
docs.text:
with container.override(Database, fake_db):
    ...
  • It works for keys bound with a factory, and with allow_override=False.
  • It only changes that key. Other singletons stay as they are.
  • It is visible to the current task or thread and to what they start (create_task, to_thread), not to other concurrent tests or requests.
  • Services that depend on the key, directly or not, are rebuilt inside the block with the override.
  • The value you pass is returned as is.

See Overrides. Limits are listed under Known limitations.

docs.title: @inject and Inject
docs.text:
• Exceptions raised by your own function are no longer wrapped in InjectionError. They pass through unchanged. Only a failure to resolve a parameter raises InjectionError, and the message names the parameter.
  • The injection plan is built on the first call, so forward references and postponed annotations (from __future__ import annotations) work.
  • Supported: sync and async functions, generators and async generators (resolved on the first next()), @classmethod and @staticmethod in either order, functools.partial and callable objects.
  • Inject[T] is a plain marker. repr() has no side effects. Equality and hash are by value. There is no caching and no isinstance spoofing.
  • Outside @inject, an Inject[T] default resolves when you read an attribute on it, from the current container, each time.
  • An Inject[...] marker on a parameter wins over a bound key that matches the parameter name. An Inject[...] that cannot be resolved raises.
# Before (0.5)
@inject
def handler(repo: Repo):
    raise ValueError("bad input")
try:
    handler()
except InjectionError:        # your ValueError arrived wrapped
    ...

# After (0.6)
try:
    handler()
except ValueError:            # your exception, unchanged
    ...

docs.title: Resolution rules
docs.text:
• Classes without __init__ are auto-resolved. int, str and other builtins, and Enum classes, are not. An abstract class with no binding raises DependencyNotFoundError.
  • A required parameter with no annotation, or a forward reference that cannot be resolved, raises InjectionError at the first resolve.
  • A parameter default is used only when the parameter's own key is not bound. try_get follows the same rule.
  • An exception raised by a constructor or factory is wrapped in InjectionError once, for the class that failed, not once per level. InjectQ's own errors (CircularDependencyError, ScopeError, ...) pass through unchanged.
  • invoke() and ainvoke() read resolved type hints, so postponed annotations work. A missing nested dependency is reported, not swallowed. ainvoke awaits async partials and callable objects.

docs.title: validate() and compile()
docs.text:
• container.validate() reports circular dependencies and accepts parameters that have defaults or allow_none. It raises InjectionError listing every problem. A factory whose parameters the container cannot fill (call-time arguments) is skipped by validate() and compile(); resolving it with get()/aget()/@inject raises.
  • container.compile() builds every resolver now and raises on the first set of errors. Call it at startup to fail fast.
  • get_dependency_graph() includes factory-bound keys and applies the lookup-by-name rule.

docs.title: Decorators and modules
docs.text:
• @singleton, @transient, @scoped, @register_as and @resource work with and without arguments: @scoped and @scoped("request").
  • A bare @scoped means the "request" scope.
  • @resource binds the resource into the container, under the type in its return annotation. Transient resources are rejected.
  • @provider(scope=...) sets the scope of a provider method.
  • ProviderModule scans the class dictionary, so properties are not evaluated. Providers are installed in definition order. Errors in a provider are raised, not swallowed. Async providers are awaited by aget.
  • ConfigurationModule, SimpleModule and Module.configure(binder) are unchanged. binder.bind_factory(..., scope=...) is new.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• A resource is initialised once, even under concurrency.
  • Teardown errors are raised, not swallowed. All teardowns run first, then the errors are raised together as an ExceptionGroup (Python 3.11+). On Python 3.10 you get the first error, with the others in its __notes__.
  • container.shutdown() and await container.ashutdown() tear down in reverse order of initialisation. Pass an exception to hand it to the teardown code.
  • Two resources with the same function name in different modules no longer replace each other.

See Scopes and resources.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
• DependencyProfiler.start() keeps old data. reset() clears it. stop() keeps data too.
  • Using a profiler in a with block attaches it to all containers.
  • The metrics buffer is bounded, so a long run does not grow without limit.
  • InjectQ.test_mode() also sets the container as the current context container.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• Errors are raised. They are no longer logged first and then raised.
  • InjectQMCPMiddleware no longer subclasses the FastMCP Middleware class. setup_fastmcp appends it to the server.
  • injectq.integrations loads lazily. Importing one integration never imports another framework.

docs.title: Things that now raise
docs.text: Situation Raises Fix Resolve a request-scoped key outside with container.scope("request") ScopeError Enter a scope, or use a framework integration Enter a scope name that is not request, action or registered ScopeError container.register_scope("name") container.get(Key) where Key needs an async factory InjectionError await container.aget(Key) A required constructor parameter has no annotation and no default InjectionError (first resolve) Add a type hint or a default A forward reference in a constructor cannot be resolved InjectionError (first resolve) Make the name importable at runtime An Inject[...] marker cannot be resolved InjectionError Bind the type An abstract class or protocol with no binding DependencyNotFoundError Bind an implementation Circular dependency CircularDependencyError (at first resolve, validate() or compile()) Break the cycle bind_factory over a class binding with allow_override=False AlreadyRegisteredError Use override() in tests, or allow overrides A resource teardown fails ExceptionGroup (3.11+) or the first error (3.10) Fix the teardown A scope used after it exited ScopeError Resolve inside the block No container found inside an integration InjectionError Call setup_fastapi, setup_fastmcp or setup_taskiq register_scope("singleton") ScopeError Pick another name

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• While any override() is active, that container resolves through slower guarded closures. This only matters in tests.
  • An override does not change objects that already hold the old value. A singleton built before the override keeps its old dependency. Inside the block, container.get(Service) builds a new Service with the override.
  • Free-threaded CPython is not tested.
  • On Python 3.15 the fastmcp extra cannot be installed yet, because one of its dependencies (rpds-py) does not build there.

docs.title: What is new
docs.text:
See the Changelog for the full list of additions: the new resolver engine, typed get/aget, InjectQ(debug=True), context-local overrides, scope exit stacks and shutdown(), scoped factories and providers, InjectFastMCP, injectq.utils.graph, and attach_profiler().

One typing caveat: an abstract class as the key trips mypy's type-abstract check. Use # type: ignore[type-abstract] or a string or Protocol key.

docs.title: injectq 0.6: guide for AI coding agents
docs.text:
injectq is a Python dependency injection container (Python 3.10+, github.com/10xhub/injectq). You bind types to classes, factories or instances in an InjectQ container and resolve them with container.get(T) / await container.aget(T), constructor injection, or @inject. Scopes (singleton, transient, request, custom) control lifetime. Extras: injectq[fastapi], injectq[taskiq], injectq[fastmcp] (fastmcp >= 2.14).

Do not migrate an app that already uses another container unless asked.

docs.title: 1. Recommended structure
docs.text:
1. One InjectQ() per application, built once at startup in a single composition root (a build_container() function or Module classes). Do not scatter @singleton decorators across files in a large app: bindings become invisible and import-order dependent.
  2. Bind by type: container.bind(Repo, SqlRepo). Use string keys only for plain config values (container.bind_instance("db_url", "...")).
  3. Constructor injection inside the app: classes declare dependencies as typed __init__ parameters; the container builds them. Use @inject only at boundaries (entry-point functions, CLI commands, callbacks you cannot construct).
  4. Scope choice: singleton for shared stateless or thread-safe things (config, pools, clients); transient for cheap stateless objects (default for factories); request (one with container.scope("request") block) for per-request state and per-request resources. A singleton must never depend on a request-scoped service.
  5. Async code uses await container.aget(T); sync code uses container.get(T). A key with an async factory or async resource needs aget.
  6. Web/worker frameworks: call setup_fastapi / setup_taskiq / setup_fastmcp once; they make your container current and open a "request" scope per request/message/task.
  7. At startup call container.validate() or container.compile() to fail fast. At shutdown call container.shutdown() or await container.ashutdown() (async resources need the async form).
  8. Tests: with container.override(Key, fake): ... for one dependency, isolated_container() / container_fixture() for a clean container. Never mutate the production container's bindings in tests.

Minimal composition root:

from injectq import InjectQ, inject


class Settings:
    def __init__(self, dsn: str = "sqlite://") -> None:
        self.dsn = dsn


class Repo:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
        self.settings = settings


class Service:
    def __init__(self, repo: Repo) -> None:
        self.repo = repo


def build_container() -> InjectQ:
    c = InjectQ()
    c.bind(Settings)            # binds Settings to itself, singleton
    c.bind(Repo)
    c.bind(Service, scope="transient")
    c.validate()                # fail fast on missing dependencies
    return c


container = build_container()


@inject(container=container)    # explicit container: no global state
def main(service: Service) -> str:
    return service.repo.settings.dsn


assert main() == "sqlite://"

docs.title: 2. Core API
docs.text: Imports: from injectq import .... Names below exist in 0.6.0.

docs.title: Container and constructor
docs.text:
InjectQ(modules: list | None = None, use_async_scopes=<deprecated, ignored, warns>, thread_safe=<deprecated, ignored, warns>,
        allow_override: bool = True, *, debug: bool = False)
InjectQ.get_instance() -> InjectQ        # current context container, else the global one
InjectQ.reset_instance() -> None         # drop the global container
InjectQ.test_mode()                      # classmethod context manager: fresh container, global + current

thread_safe= and use_async_scopes= are deprecated: accepted, ignored, and they emit DeprecationWarning. Do not add them. No locking is needed around the container.

allow_override=False: a second registration of a key raises AlreadyRegisteredError (an override() is still allowed).

docs.title: Binding
docs.text:
c.bind(service_type, implementation=<itself>, scope="singleton", to=None,
       allow_none=False, allow_concrete=True)
c.bind_instance(service_type, instance, allow_none=False, allow_concrete=True)
c.bind_factory(service_type, factory, scope="transient")   # factory params are injected; async def allowed
c[key] = SomeClass | instance | None                       # class -> singleton binding, else instance
c.factories[key] = factory                                 # dict-style factory binding
c.install_module(module)                                   # module.configure(ModuleBinder(c))
del c[key]                                                 # KeyError if unbound
key in c ; c.has(key)
c.clear()                                                  # all bindings and cached instances

scope is "singleton", "transient", "request", "action", a registered name, or a ScopeType member. Abstract classes cannot be bound as their own implementation (BindingError).

docs.title: Resolving
docs.text:
c.get(key) / c[key]                      # sync; InjectionError if an async factory is needed
await c.aget(key)                        # sync and async graphs
c.try_get(key, default=None) ; await c.atry_get(key, default=None)
c.get_factory(key) -> callable           # raw factory ; await c.aget_factory(key)
c.call_factory(key, *args, **kw)         # you supply all args ; await c.acall_factory(...)
c.invoke(key, *args, **kw)               # factory: your kwargs + remaining params injected
await c.ainvoke(key, *args, **kw)

Typed via @overload: get(type[T]) -> T; get(str) -> Any; aget likewise; try_get(type[T]) -> T | None; try_get(type[T], default: D) -> T | D; string keys -> Any. mypy caveat: passing an abstract class (ABC/Protocol) as the key triggers mypy's type-abstract check; add # type: ignore[type-abstract] on that call or bind and resolve a concrete type.

invoke injection order for params you did not pass: parameter name as a bound key, then type annotation (non-builtin), then default; else error. Pass explicit values as keyword arguments.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
Instances, string keys, factories with scope:

from injectq import InjectQ

c = InjectQ()
c.bind_instance("db_url", "postgres://x")        # also c["db_url"] = "..."

class Conn:
    def __init__(self, db_url: str) -> None:     # parameter NAME matches a bound key
        self.db_url = db_url

def make_conn(db_url: str) -> Conn:              # factory params are injected too
    return Conn(db_url)

c.bind_factory(Conn, make_conn)                  # default scope: transient
c.bind_factory(Conn, make_conn, scope="singleton")  # later registration wins
assert c.get(Conn).db_url == "postgres://x"

Async factory (must use aget):

import asyncio
from injectq import InjectQ, InjectionError

class Client: ...

async def make_client() -> Client:
    return Client()

async def main() -> None:
    c = InjectQ()
    c.bind_factory(Client, make_client, scope="singleton")
    try:
        c.get(Client)                    # raises: needs aget()
    except InjectionError:
        pass
    assert await c.aget(Client) is await c.aget(Client)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text:
@inject                                   # bare
@inject(container=c)                      # explicit container (default: InjectQ.get_instance() at call time)
Inject[T]                                 # parameter default marker; T may be a type or a string key

@singleton / @singleton(container=c)
@transient / @transient(container=c)
@scoped / @scoped("request") / @scoped(scope="job", container=c)    # bare = "request"
@register_as(ServiceType, scope="singleton", container=None)        # no bare form

@resource / @resource("request") / @resource(scope="request", container=c)
managed_resource(factory, cleanup)        # context manager
async_managed_resource(factory, cleanup)  # async context manager
get_resource_manager() -> ResourceManager # .shutdown_all(), .shutdown_all_async(); prefer container.shutdown()

@inject supports sync and async functions, generators, async generators, @classmethod/@staticmethod (either order), functools.partial, callable objects. Lookup order per parameter not passed by the caller: Inject[...] marker, bound parameter name, annotation, default.

from injectq import InjectQ, Inject, inject

class Mailer:
    def send(self) -> str:
        return "sent"

c = InjectQ()
c.bind(Mailer)
c.bind_instance("greeting", "hi")

@inject(container=c)
def handler(mailer: Mailer, greeting: str, extra: int = 5) -> str:
    # mailer: by annotation. greeting: by bound parameter name. extra: default (no key bound).
    return f"{greeting} {mailer.send()} {extra}"

@inject(container=c)
async def ahandler(m: Mailer = Inject[Mailer]) -> str:   # explicit marker, wins over name lookup
    return m.send()

assert handler() == "hi sent 5"
assert handler(extra=6) == "hi sent 6"          # passed args are never overridden

Without container=, @inject uses InjectQ.get_instance() at call time (current context container, else the global one). Prefer the explicit container= or container.context() in libraries and tests.

Class decorators bind into the container current at decoration time (InjectQ.get_instance()), or pass container=:

from injectq import InjectQ, singleton, transient, scoped, register_as

c = InjectQ()

class Repo: ...

@singleton(container=c)
class Config: ...

@transient(container=c)
class Handler: ...

@scoped("request", container=c)          # bare @scoped means "request"
class Ctx: ...

@register_as(Repo, container=c)          # register an implementation under a type
class SqlRepo(Repo): ...

assert isinstance(c.get(Repo), SqlRepo)

docs.title: Modules and providers
docs.text:
class M(Module):                 # abstract: implement configure(self, binder: ModuleBinder)
SimpleModule()                   # .bind(...), .bind_instance(...), .bind_factory(...) fluent
ConfigurationModule({key: value})   # binds each as an instance
class P(ProviderModule):         # methods marked @provider
    @provider                    # transient
    @provider(scope="singleton")
    def make(self, dep: Dep) -> Thing: ...      # return annotation required (BindingError otherwise)
ModuleBinder.bind / bind_instance / bind_factory(scope=...)

from injectq import InjectQ, Module, ProviderModule, provider, ModuleBinder

class Db: ...
class Repo:
    def __init__(self, db: Db) -> None:
        self.db = db

class CoreModule(Module):
    def configure(self, binder: ModuleBinder) -> None:
        binder.bind(Db)
        binder.bind_instance("env", "prod")

class RepoModule(ProviderModule):
    @provider(scope="singleton")           # default scope for @provider is transient
    def repo(self, db: Db) -> Repo:         # return annotation is the key
        return Repo(db)

c = InjectQ(modules=[CoreModule(), RepoModule()])
assert c.get(Repo).db is c.get(Db)

docs.title: Other exported names
docs.text:
• Exceptions (all subclass InjectQError): DependencyNotFoundError, CircularDependencyError, BindingError, InjectionError, ScopeError, AlreadyRegisteredError, ResourceError.
  • Types: Scope, ScopeType (SINGLETON, TRANSIENT, REQUEST, ACTION), ServiceKey, ServiceFactory, Factory, AsyncFactory, Provider, AsyncProvider, ResourceProvider, AsyncResourceProvider, Injectable, Configurable, ScopeAware, logger.
  • Lazily loaded on first access: injectq.testing, DependencyProfiler, DependencyValidator, DependencyVisualizer.

docs.title: Scopes and current container
docs.text:
c.scope(name) -> context manager          # sync block
c.async_scope(name) -> async context manager
c.register_scope(name: str)               # custom names only; "request" and "action" exist
c.current_exit_stack(name)                # ExitStack / AsyncExitStack of the active scope; push cleanups
c.clear_scope(name) ; c.clear_all_scopes()   # drops instances, runs no teardown
c.context()                               # with-block: make c the current container
c.activate() -> Token                     # current task/thread + children; undo with ContainerContext.reset_current(token)

ContainerContext: get_current(), set_current(c) -> token, reset_current(token), clear_current(), use(c) (sync cm), use_async(c) (async cm).

import asyncio
from injectq import InjectQ, ScopeError

c = InjectQ()

class Session: ...

c.bind(Session, scope="request")

with c.scope("request"):
    assert c.get(Session) is c.get(Session)    # one per block
try:
    c.get(Session)                              # outside a block
except ScopeError:
    pass

async def main() -> None:
    async with c.async_scope("request"):        # use when teardown is async
        assert await c.aget(Session) is c.get(Session)

c.register_scope("job")                         # custom names must be registered
with c.scope("job"):
    pass

asyncio.run(main())

Request scope is per with block: two blocks give two instances; nested same-name scopes restore the outer one; the block name must equal the binding's scope name.

docs.title: Resources (setup/teardown)
docs.text:
@resource function forms: generator / async generator (code after yield is teardown and receives the exception), function returning a (async) context manager, plain function. The key is the annotated return type (Iterator[X] -> X); without annotation, the function itself. Scope default is singleton (closed by shutdown()); @resource("request") is closed when the request scope exits. @resource("transient") raises ResourceError.

from collections.abc import Iterator
from injectq import InjectQ, resource

c = InjectQ()
events: list[str] = []

class Pool: ...
class Session: ...

@resource(container=c)                    # singleton: closed by shutdown()
def pool() -> Iterator[Pool]:
    events.append("open pool")
    try:
        yield Pool()
    finally:
        events.append("close pool")

@resource("request", container=c)         # closed when the request scope exits
def session(pool: Pool) -> Iterator[Session]:
    events.append("open session")
    try:
        yield Session()
    finally:
        events.append("close session")

with c.scope("request"):
    c.get(Session)
c.shutdown()
assert events == ["open pool", "open session", "close session", "close pool"]

Shutdown: container.shutdown(exc=None) (sync resources) / await container.ashutdown(exc=None) (sync and async resources), reverse order of creation. Teardown errors are raised after all teardowns ran (ExceptionGroup on 3.11+, first error with __notes__ on 3.10). container.track_resource(key, lifecycle) is advanced use.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
The current container, the active scopes and the active override layer each live in a ContextVar. Each asyncio task runs in a copy of the context it was created from:

  • A change made inside a task is not seen by other tasks.
  • A change made before a task starts is seen by that task.
  • Two tasks can use two containers at the same time without leaking.

InjectQ.get_instance() returns the current container, else the global one.

docs.title: Making a container current
docs.text:
import asyncio
from injectq import ContainerContext, InjectQ

container = InjectQ()

with container.context():                      # preferred: always restores
    assert InjectQ.get_instance() is container


async def main() -> None:
    async with ContainerContext.use_async(container):
        assert InjectQ.get_instance() is container


asyncio.run(main())

token = container.activate()                   # no with-block: keep the token
try:
    assert InjectQ.get_instance() is container
finally:
    ContainerContext.reset_current(token)

ContainerContext.set_current(c) equals activate() and returns a token. clear_current() sets None and cannot restore an outer value: prefer tokens. Activate before starting tasks; already-running sibling tasks do not see it.

docs.title: Tasks and threads
docs.text:
How code runs Sees caller's container, scope, override? await asyncio.create_task(...) Yes (context copied at creation) await asyncio.to_thread(...) Yes anyio.to_thread.run_sync (FastAPI sync routes) Yes loop.run_in_executor(None, ...) No: global container, no scope threading.Thread(...) No: global container, no scope a task that was already running when you called activate() No

Fixes for run_in_executor / plain threads:

import asyncio
import contextvars
from injectq import InjectQ

container = InjectQ()
container.bind_instance("name", "x")


def work() -> str:
    return InjectQ.get_instance().get("name")      # container must be current here


async def main() -> None:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    with container.context():
        # 1. copy the context into the executor
        ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
        assert await loop.run_in_executor(None, ctx.run, work) == "x"
        # 2. or use asyncio.to_thread, which copies for you
        assert await asyncio.to_thread(work) == "x"


def work_explicit() -> str:
    with container.context():                       # 3. or activate inside the thread
        return InjectQ.get_instance().get("name")


asyncio.run(main())
assert work_explicit() == "x"

Scopes follow the same rule: a with container.scope("request") block is visible to tasks and to_thread calls started inside it, not to run_in_executor or plain threads (a request-scoped resolve there raises ScopeError). A scope belongs to one container.

docs.title: aget rules
docs.text:
• Async code: await container.aget(T). It honours scopes and returns the same singleton as get().
  • get() on a key whose graph needs an async factory or async resource raises InjectionError. If the async part is already a cached singleton/scoped instance, get() works.
  • Use async with container.async_scope(...) when teardown is async (async @resource, async callbacks on the exit stack). In a plain with container.scope(...) the exit stack is a sync ExitStack.
  • Integrations resolve with aget (InjectFastAPI, InjectTaskiq, InjectFastMCP).
  • @inject on an async def function (or async generator) resolves its parameters with aget, so async factories work there. A sync def under @inject uses get().
  • A singleton is created once even if many tasks/threads ask at once; async factories share one future between awaiters.

docs.title: Threads and singletons
docs.text: Reads take no lock; creation takes a per-key lock. Singletons are shared by all threads and tasks, so they must be safe to share. Put per-request mutable state in @scoped("request"). Do not call asyncio.run inside a handler to resolve async keys; use aget.

docs.title: 5. Framework integrations
docs.text:
Install the extra: pip install "injectq[fastapi]", "injectq[taskiq]" or "injectq[fastmcp]". Each integration imports its framework only when its functions are called. Each makes your container the current container and opens one "request" scope per HTTP request / WebSocket connection (FastAPI), MCP message (FastMCP) or task (Taskiq). Request-scoped services and @resource("request") resources are created and torn down per unit of work.

Inside a handler, InjectQ.get_instance() and @inject use the container you passed to setup_*, not the global one.

Public names (injectq.integrations.<fastapi|taskiq|fastmcp>):

  • setup_fastapi(container, app), InjectFastAPI(T), get_container_fastapi(connection=None), InjectQRequestMiddleware
  • setup_taskiq(container, broker), InjectTaskiq(T), get_container_taskiq(state=None), InjectQTaskiqMiddleware
  • setup_fastmcp(container, mcp), InjectFastMCP(T), get_container_fastmcp(), InjectQMCPMiddleware

docs.title: FastAPI
docs.text:
Route parameter: Annotated[T, InjectFastAPI(T)].

from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from injectq import InjectQ, scoped
from injectq.integrations.fastapi import InjectFastAPI, setup_fastapi

container = InjectQ()
app = FastAPI()
setup_fastapi(container, app)           # once, at startup


@scoped(container=container)            # bare/"request": one per HTTP request
class RequestCtx:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls = 0


class Greeter:
    def __init__(self, ctx: RequestCtx) -> None:
        self.ctx = ctx

    def greet(self) -> str:
        self.ctx.calls += 1
        return f"hello {self.ctx.calls}"


container.bind(Greeter, scope="request")


@app.get("/hi")
async def hi(g: Annotated[Greeter, InjectFastAPI(Greeter)]):
    return {"msg": g.greet()}


@app.get("/sync")
def sync_route(g: Annotated[Greeter, InjectFastAPI(Greeter)]):   # sync routes work (anyio thread copies context)
    return {"msg": g.greet()}


with TestClient(app) as client:
    assert client.get("/hi").json() == {"msg": "hello 1"}
    assert client.get("/hi").json() == {"msg": "hello 1"}     # new request, new scope
    assert client.get("/sync").json() == {"msg": "hello 1"}
  • InjectFastAPI(T) returns a Depends; it awaits container.aget(T), so async factories and async resources work.
  • Shutdown: call await container.ashutdown() in the lifespan handler:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
from injectq import InjectQ

container = InjectQ()


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    yield
    await container.ashutdown()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
  • get_container_fastapi(request) returns the container (current one, else the one stored on app.state).
  • Middleware is pure ASGI (InjectQRequestMiddleware), handles http and websocket, passes lifespan through.
  • Do not resolve request-scoped services in lifespan/startup code (no request scope there: ScopeError).
  • Background tasks run after the response; the request scope may be closed by then. Resolve what you need before scheduling them.

docs.title: Taskiq
docs.text:
Task parameter: Annotated[T, InjectTaskiq(T)].

import asyncio
from typing import Annotated
from taskiq import InMemoryBroker
from injectq import InjectQ
from injectq.integrations.taskiq import InjectTaskiq, setup_taskiq


class Mailer:
    def send(self, to: str) -> str:
        return f"sent to {to}"


container = InjectQ()
container.bind(Mailer)
broker = InMemoryBroker()
setup_taskiq(container, broker)


@broker.task
async def welcome(to: str, mailer: Annotated[Mailer, InjectTaskiq(Mailer)]) -> str:
    return mailer.send(to)


async def main() -> None:
    await broker.startup()
    task = await welcome.kiq("a@b.c")
    result = await task.wait_result()
    assert result.return_value == "sent to a@b.c"
    await broker.shutdown()


asyncio.run(main())
  • Use async def tasks. A plain def task body runs in loop.run_in_executor: there InjectQ.get_instance() and @inject use the global container, and request-scoped keys raise ScopeError. InjectTaskiq(...) parameters still work because they resolve on the event loop before the body.
  • Scope teardown (@resource("request")) runs after the task and sees the task exception. Scope-closing errors are logged, not raised (so Taskiq can still store the result).
  • The container is also on broker.state.injectq_container. Call setup_taskiq on the worker-side broker module.

docs.title: FastMCP
docs.text:
Tool parameter: x: T = InjectFastMCP(T).

# no-run: requires a running MCP server/client to exercise
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from injectq import InjectQ, scoped
from injectq.integrations.fastmcp import InjectFastMCP, setup_fastmcp

container = InjectQ()
mcp = FastMCP("demo")
setup_fastmcp(container, mcp)


class Users:
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        return ["a"]


container.bind(Users)


@mcp.tool
async def list_users(users: Users = InjectFastMCP(Users)) -> list[str]:
    return users.names()
  • InjectFastMCP(T) parameters are hidden from the MCP tool schema.
  • setup_fastmcp adds InjectQMCPMiddleware with mcp.add_middleware; it does not subclass FastMCP's Middleware.
  • One "request" scope per MCP message (tool call, resource read, prompt, listing).
  • get_container_fastmcp() returns the container; raises InjectionError outside a request when nothing is stored on the server.

docs.title: Testing integrations
docs.text:
• FastAPI: TestClient(app); bind fakes before the request, or wrap the client calls in with container.override(Key, fake): (a route behind InjectFastAPI sees the override).
  • Taskiq: InMemoryBroker() as above.
  • FastMCP: use fastmcp.Client(mcp) in-memory transport.

docs.title: 6. Testing
docs.text: Tools: container.override, InjectQ.test_mode(), injectq.testing.isolated_container, container_fixture, override_dependency, MockModule.

docs.title: override: swap one dependency
docs.text:
from injectq import InjectQ


class Mailer:
    def send(self) -> str:
        return "real"


class FakeMailer(Mailer):
    def send(self) -> str:
        return "fake"


class Notifier:
    def __init__(self, mailer: Mailer) -> None:
        self.mailer = mailer


class Api:
    def __init__(self, notifier: Notifier) -> None:
        self.notifier = notifier


container = InjectQ()
container.bind(Mailer)
container.bind(Notifier)
container.bind(Api)

fake = FakeMailer()
with container.override(Mailer, fake):
    assert container.get(Api).notifier.mailer is fake       # transitive: Api -> Notifier -> Mailer
assert type(container.get(Api).notifier.mailer) is Mailer    # restored

Rules:

  • The value is returned as is (no copy, no call). Pass the object, not a class or factory.
  • Transitive: services depending on the key (directly or not) are rebuilt with it inside the block.
  • Works for class bindings, instances, factory-bound keys, string keys, and allow_override=False containers.
  • Context-local: visible to the current task/thread and to create_task / to_thread started inside. Not visible to run_in_executor, plain threads, or concurrent tests.
  • Nests: inner wins; leaving restores the outer.
  • Only that key changes. Singletons built before the block keep their old dependencies (a Notifier singleton built earlier keeps the real Mailer); inside the block get(Notifier) builds a fresh one. Use isolated_container() for a fully fresh container.
  • While any override is active, that container resolves through slower guarded closures and source() returns None. Fine for tests.

override_dependency(key, value, container=None) is the same as a function; it defaults to the global container.

docs.title: Fresh container per test
docs.text:
from injectq import InjectQ, singleton
from injectq.testing import isolated_container


def test_it() -> None:
    with isolated_container() as c:                 # same as InjectQ.test_mode()
        @singleton                                   # decorator binds into the current container: c
        class Thing: ...

        assert c.get(Thing) is InjectQ.get_instance().get(Thing)


test_it()

isolated_container() makes the new container both the global instance and the current context container, then restores both. @inject, @singleton and InjectQ.get_instance() therefore use it.

docs.title: pytest
docs.text:
# conftest.py
from injectq.testing import container_fixture

container = container_fixture()              # a fixture named "container"
di = container_fixture(name="di")            # custom fixture name

# test_x.py
def test_notifier(container):
    container.bind(Mailer, FakeMailer)
    ...

Async tests need pytest-asyncio (or anyio's pytest plugin); use await container.aget(...). For a shared production container built by build_container(), build a new one per test then c.override(...) or bind fakes into that fresh container. Never share mutable test state through a module-level container. Always call shutdown()/ashutdown() in fixture teardown so resources do not leak between tests.

docs.title: MockModule
docs.text:
MockModule().mock(T, **attrs) binds a mock of T (attributes from kwargs); bind_value(key, value) binds a fixed value; both return self. create_test_module({key: value}) builds a module from a dict. Also exported: MockFactory, mock_factory.

from injectq import InjectQ
from injectq.testing import MockModule


class Db:
    def query(self) -> str:
        return "real"


c = InjectQ()
c.install_module(MockModule().mock(Db).bind_value("env", "test"))
assert c.get("env") == "test"
assert c.get(Db) is c.get(Db)             # bound as an instance

docs.title: 7. Rules and pitfalls
docs.text:
Things that raise in 0.6, with the fix:

Mistake Raises Fix container.get(K) where K needs an async factory/resource InjectionError ("use aget()") await container.aget(K). Use aget in async code by default. Resolve a "request"-scoped key outside with container.scope("request") ScopeError Enter a scope, or use a framework integration. Do not "fix" by making it a singleton. container.scope("name") for a name that is not request/action/registered ScopeError: Unknown scope container.register_scope("name") once. Scoped key bound to "request" but block is a different name ScopeError Block name must equal the binding's scope name. Required constructor param with no annotation and no default InjectionError at first resolve Add a type hint or a default. Abstract class/protocol with no binding DependencyNotFoundError Bind a concrete implementation (bind(Abstract, Abstract) raises BindingError). Cycles raise CircularDependencyError; validate() finds both early. @resource("transient") ResourceError Use singleton or a named scope. Integration helper used without a setup_* call InjectionError Call setup_*. bind/bind_factory on an existing key with InjectQ(allow_override=False) AlreadyRegisteredError Bind once, or use override() in tests. @inject on a class InjectionError at decoration Put @inject on a function; classes use constructor injection.

Behaviour traps (no exception, wrong result):

  • The current container and scopes are ContextVars: plain threading.Thread and loop.run_in_executor do not see them, and already-running sibling tasks do not see a later activate() (section 4).
  • Sync Taskiq task bodies run in run_in_executor: get_instance() and @inject there use the global container. Use async def tasks.
  • override() is local to the current context, slows resolution while active, and does not change objects that already hold the old value (see section 6).
  • Parameter defaults are used only when the parameter's own key (by type, or name) is not bound. A bound key always beats the default.
  • Inject[T] marker beats a bound parameter name. An unresolvable Inject[...] raises; it never passes through as a value.
  • Last registration wins for a key, whatever kind. Rebinding drops that key's cached singleton. bind_factory is transient by default (called on every resolve): add scope="singleton" to cache.
  • Exceptions raised by your own @inject function pass through unchanged. Only resolution failures are InjectionError. Constructor errors during resolution are wrapped in InjectionError once, for the class that failed; injectq's own errors are not wrapped.
  • InjectQ(debug=True) disables generated code (slower, simpler tracebacks): keep it off in production.

Do not write deprecated or removed names (test_container, TestModule, pytest_container_fixture, InjectAPI, InjectTask, InjectMCP, setup_mcp, get_container_mcp, get_injector_instance_taskiq, injectq.components, thread_safe=, use_async_scopes=, the scope names "async_request"/"async_action"). Section 10 has the replacements. Run tests with pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning to find them.

Limitations to tell the user about:

  • Wiring errors surface at first resolve unless you call validate() or compile() at startup.
  • Bindings are type-keyed: two bindings of one type need distinct keys (a subclass, a wrapper class or a string key).
  • override(), an attached profiler and debug=True use slower resolution paths. Generated resolvers are harder to step through (use debug=True).
  • Free-threaded CPython is not tested; the fastmcp extra cannot be installed on Python 3.15 yet.

docs.title: 8. Performance
docs.text:
get() of a cached singleton and building small graphs are sub-microsecond on a warmed container. Median microseconds per operation, CPython 3.13, same machine for all libraries; hand-written means plain constructor calls with no container. Scenarios: S1 cached singleton, S2 transient chain C(B(A())), S3 wide graph (5 transients over 5 singletons), S4 request scope enter/resolve/exit, S5 @inject call with 3 singletons, S6 async S2.

µs/op (median, lower is better) S1 singleton S2 transient chain S3 wide graph S4 request scope S5 injected call S6 async chain injectq 0.083 0.302 0.550 0.968 0.143 0.427 aioinject [1] 0.295 0.787 1.768 2.278 n/a 0.992 dependency-injector [2] 0.057 1.203 3.038 n/a 1.127 37.8 dishka [3] 0.307 0.516 1.069 1.526 1.165 1.068 diwire [4] 0.424 0.609 0.884 4.609 6.820 0.874 inject [5] 0.158 4.785 12.2 n/a 2.462 n/a injector [6] 1.331 42.7 90.6 14.4 16.8 n/a kink [7] 0.168 3.688 12.6 n/a 2.366 n/a lagom [8] 0.155 5.624 12.0 n/a 1.474 n/a punq [9] 1.097 36.5 90.6 n/a n/a n/a rodi [10] 0.290 0.758 1.852 0.836 1.056 n/a svcs [11] 0.189 2.590 8.087 1.940 n/a 3.068 that-depends [12] 0.077 0.938 3.479 24.7 3.163 1.569 wireup [13] 0.092 0.512 1.434 1.130 0.269 0.676 hand-written (floor) 0.019 0.166 0.355 0.345 0.041 0.229 injectq rank 3 of 14 1 of 14 1 of 14 2 of 9 1 of 11 1 of 8 fastest DI library dependency-injector injectq injectq rodi injectq injectq

Bold: fastest DI library in the column (hand-written excluded). n/a: the library has no such feature.

Setup notes per library ([1]-[13]) [1] **aioinject**: sync `SyncContainer` for S1-S5/S7, async `Container` for S6; transients registered in the lifetime scope to resolve from the root context. n/a: S5 no generic injection decorator (per-framework `inject` only). [2] **dependency-injector**: S6 uses providers in async mode. n/a: S4 no enter/exit request scope (only context-local singletons, a different mechanism). [3] **dishka**: no transient lifetime; `cache=False` is its equivalent. [4] **diwire**: default `SCOPED` lifetime at the root scope = singleton; transient via `Lifetime.TRANSIENT`; S5 passes `diwire_resolver=` explicitly. [5] **inject**: one global injector; singletons via `bind_to_constructor`, transients via `bind_to_provider`, constructors wired with `autoparams`. n/a: S4 no request scope; S6 no async resolution. [6] **injector**: request scope is a custom `Scope` subclass (cache swapped on enter/exit); constructors need `@inject` (applied to the benchmark classes). n/a: S6 no async API. [7] **kink**: `@inject` on a class registers it (singleton; `use_factory=True` = transient) and mutates `__init__`; S7 restores `__init__` before re-decorating. n/a: S4 no request scope; S6 no async resolution. [8] **lagom**: unregistered classes are autowired as transient. n/a: S4 no request scope; S6 no async resolution. [9] **punq**: transient is the default scope. n/a: S4 no request scope (only transient and singleton); S5 no injection decorator; S6 no async API. [10] **rodi**: resolved with `provider.get` / `provider.exec` (each call creates an activation scope); S7 includes `build_provider()`, which validates and wires eagerly. n/a: S6 no async resolution (sync only). [11] **svcs**: caches per `Container`, so transient = a new `Container` per operation (its construction is timed). n/a: S5 no generic injection decorator (framework integrations only). [12] **that-depends**: S5 with `@inject(scope=None)`; S4 via a `ContextResource` in `ContextScopes.REQUEST`. [13] **wireup**: transients and scoped services resolve from a scope: S2, S3, S6 use one long-lived scope, S4/S5 enter one per operation.

14 libraries, AMD Ryzen 5 5600G with Radeon Graphics, CPython 3.13.13, median of 25 repeats, 2026-11-23. Full table, chart and method: docs/benchmarks.md.

How the engine behaves:

  • Each service gets one resolver function. Singleton keys use small linked closures. A transient or scoped key starts on closures and, on its 2nd resolve, is replaced by one generated Python function that calls constructors inline.
  • A registry change (bind, rebinding, del c[key]) discards compiled code, which is rebuilt on the next resolve.
  • @inject builds its plan on the first call and reuses compiled resolvers after.

Tuning:

  • Do not micro-optimise DI: the container costs about a microsecond per request.
  • Never benchmark the first resolve of a key. Warm up with 2 resolves or call container.compile().
  • Bind everything at startup, not per request. Keep debug=True, profilers and override() out of production.
  • Reproduce numbers with python benchmarks/run.py (injectq only) or make bench-compare (cross-library). See the Benchmarks page of the docs.

docs.title: 9. Debugging
docs.text:
• container.validate() lists every unresolvable service and cycle (InjectionError) without building instances. Also: c.validate() accepts defaults and allow_none.
  • container.compile() builds all resolvers; raises on the first problem set.
  • container.get_dependency_graph() returns {key: [dependency keys]}; container.visualize_dependencies() returns a DependencyVisualizer with to_ascii(), to_dot(), to_json(), save_graph(), find_cycles(). Graph helpers also live in injectq.utils.graph (find_cycles, find_path, reachable).
  • Generated code: after container.compile(), print(container._resolver.source(Key)) shows the generated function. Returns None for singletons/instances, uncompiled keys, debug=True, an attached profiler or an active override.
  • Tracebacks through generated code show frames named <injectq-generated:Name>. Read from the top: your exception and the generated line that called your constructor, then one InjectionError for the class that failed (__cause__ is your exception).
  • InjectQ(debug=True) while developing: plain closures, steppable frames, source() returns None.
  • Time resolutions: from injectq.diagnostics import DependencyProfiler, then container.attach_profiler(p) / container.detach_profiler(). Profiler start() keeps data; reset() clears it.

docs.title: Behaviour changes (0.5 to 0.6)
docs.text:
1. The current container is per task and thread. activate() and set_current() return a token for ContainerContext.reset_current(token); with container.context(): is simpler. run_in_executor and plain threads do not inherit it. In 0.5, set_current() changed the container for every task on the thread.
  2. In FastAPI, FastMCP and Taskiq, InjectQ.get_instance() and @inject use the container passed to setup_* (0.5 used the global one). Sync Taskiq task bodies are the exception.
  3. Request scope is per with block. A request-scoped key outside a block raises ScopeError (0.5 returned an instance); two blocks give two instances; nested same-name scopes restore the outer one.
  4. register_scope(name) takes only a name (0.5: container._scope_manager.register_scope("job", JobScope())). Unknown scope names raise ScopeError.
  5. aget() honours scopes and returns the same singleton as get(). Singletons are created once under concurrency.
  6. get() on a key that needs an async factory raises InjectionError (0.5 returned a coroutine).
  7. One provider map: the later registration of a key wins whatever its kind (0.5: a factory always won). Rebinding drops the cached singleton.
  8. override() is context-local, transitive, works on factory-bound keys and does not clear other singletons.
  9. @inject does not wrap your exceptions (0.5 wrapped them in InjectionError). Plans build on first call, so forward references work. Inject[T] is a plain marker that beats a bound parameter name.
  10. Parameter defaults are used only when the parameter's own key is not bound. A required parameter with no annotation or default raises at first resolve.
  11. validate() reports cycles and lists every problem; compile() raises on errors.
  12. Decorators @singleton/@transient/@scoped/@register_as/@resource work bare and with arguments; bare @scoped is "request". @resource binds under its return annotation type.
  13. Resource teardown errors are raised after all teardowns ran. shutdown() / ashutdown() tear down in reverse order.
  14. Integration errors are raised, not logged first. InjectQMCPMiddleware no longer subclasses FastMCP's Middleware.
  15. InjectQ.test_mode() also sets the container as the current context container.

New in 0.6: generated resolvers, InjectQ(debug=True), context-local overrides, scope exit stacks (current_exit_stack, track_resource), shutdown() / ashutdown(), bind_factory(..., scope=...), ScopeError / AlreadyRegisteredError / ModuleBinder / ResourceError exported from injectq, InjectFastMCP, setup_fastmcp, get_container_taskiq, injectq.utils.graph, attach_profiler / detach_profiler.

docs.title: 11. Checklist before finishing
docs.text:
• One container, built in one place; no bindings created per request.
  • aget in async code; no get() on async factories or resources.
  • Request-scoped services are resolved only inside a scope (integration or with container.scope(...)); no singleton depends on a scoped service.
  • Type keys (string keys only for plain values); custom scope names registered.
  • Resources have teardown, and shutdown() / ashutdown() runs at exit (lifespan handler for FastAPI).
  • Nothing relies on a plain thread or run_in_executor seeing the container or a scope.
  • container.validate() or compile() runs at startup and in a test.
  • Tests use override(), isolated_container() or container_fixture(), not edits to a shared container.
  • No deprecated or removed names; pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning is clean.
  • The extra for the integration is installed (pip install "injectq[fastapi]").

docs.title: Container
docs.text:
from injectq import InjectQ

container = InjectQ()                     # a new container
container = InjectQ.get_instance()        # current context container, else the global one
container = InjectQ(
    modules=[MyModule()],                 # installed at creation
    allow_override=True,                  # False: a second registration raises AlreadyRegisteredError
    debug=False,                          # True: plain closures, simpler tracebacks
)

InjectQ.reset_instance() drops the global container. container.clear() removes all bindings and cached instances.

docs.title: Binding
docs.text:
container[Database] = PostgresDatabase        # class: singleton binding
container["db_url"] = "postgresql://..."      # anything else: an instance
container.bind(UserService)                   # bind a class to itself
container.bind(Database, PostgresDatabase, scope="request")
container.bind(OptionalService, None, allow_none=True)
container.bind_instance("config", app_config)
container.bind_factory(Database, create_database)                    # transient by default
container.bind_factory(Database, create_database, scope="singleton")
container.factories["cache"] = make_cache     # dict-style factory binding

scope is "singleton" (the default for bind), "transient" (the default for bind_factory), "request", "action", a registered name, or a ScopeType. A factory's parameters are injected like a constructor's. An async def factory needs aget(). The last registration of a key wins, and rebinding a key drops its cached singleton.

del container[key], key in container and container.has(key) work as you would expect.

docs.title: Resolving
docs.text:
service = container[UserService]              # same as container.get(UserService)
service = await container.aget(UserService)   # sync and async graphs
maybe = container.try_get(UserService)        # None if not bound (or pass a default)
maybe = await container.atry_get(UserService)

get(type[T]) returns T, and a str key returns Any. get() on a key that needs an async factory raises InjectionError: use aget().

docs.title: Factories
docs.text:
def create_pool(db: Database, size: int = 10) -> Pool: ...
container.bind_factory("pool", create_pool)

factory = container.get_factory("pool")               # the raw function
pool = container.call_factory("pool", db, size=20)    # you pass every argument
pool = container.invoke("pool", size=20)              # you pass some, the rest is injected
pool = await container.ainvoke("pool", size=20)       # also awaits async factories
factory = await container.aget_factory("pool")
pool = await container.acall_factory("pool", db)

invoke fills each parameter you did not pass from: an Inject[...] marker, a bound key equal to the parameter name, a bound key equal to a non-builtin annotation, then the default. Otherwise it raises DependencyNotFoundError. Pass explicit values by keyword.

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text:
from injectq import Inject, inject, register_as, resource, scoped, singleton, transient

@inject                                  # bare, or @inject(container=c)
def handler(service: UserService, db_url: str, db: Database = Inject[Database]): ...
handler()                                # parameters you do not pass are injected

@singleton                               # also @singleton(container=c)
class Config: ...

@transient
class Handler: ...

@scoped                                  # bare means "request"; also @scoped("job")
class Session: ...

@register_as(Repo)                       # register the class as an implementation of Repo
class SqlRepo(Repo): ...

@resource                                # singleton, closed by shutdown()
def pool() -> Iterator[Pool]:            # the key is the return annotation's type
    p = Pool()
    try:
        yield p
    finally:
        p.close()

@resource("request")                     # closed when the request scope exits
async def session() -> AsyncIterator[Session]:
    async with make_session() as s:
        yield s

Class decorators bind into InjectQ.get_instance() at decoration time unless you pass container=. @inject uses the current container at call time unless you pass container=. It supports sync and async functions, generators, classmethod/staticmethod and partials. Parameter lookup: Inject[...] marker, bound parameter name, annotation, default.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
container.bind(Session, scope="request")

with container.scope("request"):              # one block, one set of instances
    session = container[Session]
async with container.async_scope("request"):  # use when teardown is async
    session = await container.aget(Session)

container.register_scope("job")               # custom name (not "singleton" or "transient")
container.current_exit_stack("request").callback(cleanup)   # runs when the scope exits
container.clear_scope("request")              # drops instances, runs no teardown
container.clear_all_scopes()

Resolving a scoped key outside its scope raises ScopeError; so does entering an unknown scope name. ScopeType has SINGLETON, TRANSIENT, REQUEST and ACTION. See Scopes.

docs.title: Resources and shutdown
docs.text:
container.shutdown()                  # close singleton resources, last created first
await container.ashutdown()           # also awaits async resources
container.track_resource(key, lifecycle)   # advanced

Teardown errors are raised after every teardown has run: an ExceptionGroup on Python 3.11+, the first error (others in __notes__) on 3.10. See Resources.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
from injectq import ConfigurationModule, Module, ModuleBinder, ProviderModule, SimpleModule, provider

class DbModule(Module):
    def configure(self, binder: ModuleBinder) -> None:
        binder.bind(Database, PostgresDatabase)
        binder.bind_instance("db_url", "postgresql://...")
        binder.bind_factory(Pool, create_pool, scope="singleton")

class ServiceModule(ProviderModule):
    @provider(scope="singleton")          # default scope is transient
    def user_service(self, db: Database) -> UserService:   # the return annotation is the key
        return UserService(db)

simple = SimpleModule().bind(Database, PostgresDatabase).bind_instance("env", "prod")
config = ConfigurationModule({"db_url": "postgresql://..."})

container = InjectQ(modules=[DbModule(), ServiceModule()])
container.install_module(simple)

docs.title: Current container
docs.text:
from injectq import ContainerContext

with container.context():                       # same as ContainerContext.use(container)
    assert InjectQ.get_instance() is container
async with ContainerContext.use_async(container): ...

token = container.activate()                    # same as ContainerContext.set_current(container)
ContainerContext.reset_current(token)           # restore the previous container
ContainerContext.get_current()                  # the current container or None

The current container is a ContextVar: it applies to the current task or thread and to what they start afterwards (asyncio.create_task, asyncio.to_thread), not to sibling tasks. Plain threads and run_in_executor do not inherit it. See Context and concurrency.

docs.title: Overrides and testing
docs.text:
# Replace one dependency inside a block: context-local, reaches dependents
with container.override(Mailer, FakeMailer()):
    api = container.get(Api)

from injectq.testing import (
    MockModule, container_fixture, isolated_container, override_dependency,
)

with isolated_container() as c:               # fresh container, global and current
    c.install_module(MockModule().mock(Database, url="x").bind_value("env", "test"))

with override_dependency(Mailer, FakeMailer(), container=c): ...   # container.override() as a function

container = container_fixture()               # in conftest.py: a pytest fixture named "container"
di = container_fixture(name="di")             # custom fixture name

container.validate()               # raises InjectionError listing every problem (cycles, missing dependencies); skips factories with call-time arguments

print(profiler.report())
container.attach_profiler(profiler)                   # or attach to one container

docs.text:
All inherit from InjectQError.
